newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end stable, foreigners trickle into mkt.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end stable, foreigners trickle into mkt.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed broadly stable Tuesday because foreign investment dribbled back into the market and helped stocks to resist the general undertow, brokers said.
After the market's dip Monday and flat trade Tuesday, the exchange was expected to start rising slightly Wednesday as the flow of foreigners built up, they added.
Tuesday, the General Index, edged down 0.04 percent to 1,419.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.46 percent to 1,948.4 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
After foreign investors were largely absent Monday due to a national holiday in the United States, volume picked up Tuesday to 27.4 million soles ($11.1 million).
However, much of the extra trade was generated by Chilean investors who were looking to buy Edegel, which accounted for 20 percent of the session's volume, brokers said.
The electricity generating utility was attractive because investors were seeking to buy the stock before Wednesday's record date for a cash dividend of 0.1326 sol per share, they added.
"The session was stable, without anything substantial going on, except for the interest in Edegel," said Pablo Navarra at local brokerage Fortuna.

Among other leaders, benchmark Telefnica del Per climbed 1.23 percent to 5.75 soles, accounting for 15 percent of the day's trade, and brewery Backus y Johnston fell 0.41 percent to 2.43 soles on volume of 545,000 shares.
In a total of 2,122 trades, 23 stocks rose, 31 fell and 35 were stable.
